code: plot(cytb$span_start, cytb$span_end, pch = 19,      xlab = "aligned start on reference (bp)", ylab = "aligned end (bp)") abline(h = max(cytb$span_start), v = min(cytb$span_end), lty = 2) keep <- cytb[cytb$span_start < 400, ] w <- c(max(keep$span_start), min(keep$span_end)) w #> [1] 115 731 dropped <- setdiff(cytb$accession, keep$accession) dropped #> [1] "EU285251.1" "EU285250.1" window_seq <- substr(ref, w[1] + 1, w[2] + 1)   # 0-based coords -> 1-based substr m <- align_sw(window_seq, keep$sequence, scoring = c(2, -3, 5, 2)) keep$frag <- mapply(substr, keep$sequence, m$start_j + 1, m$end_j + 1) range(nchar(keep$frag)) #> [1] 605 617

title: Case study: hare cytochrome b fragments
text: Now question study: pick one reference haplotype per species ask every fragment far sits . diagonal within-species scale (0–8 edits); -diagonal entries -species scale (~55–64 within Lepus, ~100+ rabbit). barcode gap — empty interval “species” “different species” distances — whole reason cytb works marker, computed three calls.  Two honest caveats numbers surface free: Oryctolagus within group splits two mtDNA lineages (~0 ~55 edits — documented polymorphism rabbit), timidus isolate ALT2 sits ~48 edits European timidus references, divergent Asian lineage. Edit distance paper structure really .
code: pick <- function(acc) keep$frag[keep$accession == acc] refs <- c(granatensis = "JF299036.1", timidus = "LC132658.1",           europaeus = "MN098896.1", cuniculus = "AY292717.1")  for (sp in names(refs))     keep[[paste0("d_", sp)]] <-         align(keep$frag, pick(refs[sp]), smax = 511, with_cigar = FALSE)$score  d <- aggregate(cbind(d_granatensis, d_timidus, d_europaeus, d_cuniculus) ~ species,                keep, median) print(d, right = FALSE) #>   species     d_granatensis d_timidus d_europaeus d_cuniculus #> 1 cuniculus   100           118       106.0         3.5       #> 2 europaeus    55            60         2.5       106.0       #> 3 granatensis   2            62        54.0       101.0       #> 4 timidus      61             6        62.0       117.5 ids <- keep$accession within <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(keep)), function(i)     align(keep$frag[i], keep$frag[keep$species == keep$species[i] & ids != ids[i]],           smax = 511, with_cigar = FALSE)$score)) between <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(keep)), function(i)     align(keep$frag[i], keep$frag[keep$species != keep$species[i]],           smax = 511, with_cigar = FALSE)$score))  br <- seq(0, max(c(within, between)) + 5, by = 5) hw <- hist(within, breaks = br, plot = FALSE) hb <- hist(between, breaks = br, plot = FALSE) plot(hb, col = adjustcolor("tomato", 0.6), border = "white",      ylim = c(0, max(hw$counts, hb$counts)),      main = "edit distance over the 617 bp window", xlab = "edits") plot(hw, col = adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.6), border = "white", add = TRUE) legend("topleft", c("between species", "within species"),        fill = c(adjustcolor("tomato", 0.6), adjustcolor("steelblue", 0.6)))

title: Three pipeline use cases
text: -target search natural habitat bounded alignment: candidate sites matter sit within edits guide — anything beyond ~5 noise never see. smax cutoff, made explicit. planted sites resolve — 196 random candidates reported resolved = FALSE rather returned meaningless large distances. plain stringdist-style call get 200 numbers cutoff live head; part computation.
code: rand_seq <- function(n, len)     vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)         paste0(sample(c("A", "C", "G", "T"), len, replace = TRUE), collapse = ""),         character(1))  guide <- "GAGTCCGAGCAGAAGAAGAA"   # a 20-nt spacer (EMX1-like) # 200 random candidate sites; plant a handful at known distances candidates <- rand_seq(200, 20) mutate <- function(s, k) {     x <- strsplit(s, "")[[1]]     pos <- sample(seq_along(x), k)     x[pos] <- vapply(x[pos], function(b)         sample(setdiff(c("A", "C", "G", "T"), b), 1), character(1))     paste0(x, collapse = "") } planted <- c(mutate(guide, 1), mutate(guide, 2), mutate(guide, 3), mutate(guide, 4)) candidates[1:4] <- planted  hits <- align(candidates, guide, smax = 4, with_cigar = TRUE) table(hits$resolved) #>  #> FALSE  TRUE  #>   196     4 hits[hits$resolved, ] #>   score resolved                cigar rescore_ok wellformed_ok #> 1     1     TRUE MMMXMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM       TRUE          TRUE #> 2     2     TRUE MMMMMMMMXMMMXMMMMMMM       TRUE          TRUE #> 3     3     TRUE XMMMMMMMMMMXMMMMXMMM       TRUE          TRUE #> 4     4     TRUE MMMMXMMXMXMMMMMMMMMX       TRUE          TRUE

title: Three pipeline use cases
text: align_sw() answers “short motif occur anywhere read, ?” — coordinates included. clean read scores residual 9 (best random hit 80 bp); partial 3’-end adapter maps position 50; full adapter 30. start_j/end_j tell exactly trim — extra bookkeeping.
code: adapter <- "AGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTC"   # standard Illumina TruSeq adapter reads <- c(     clean   = paste0(rand_seq(1, 80)),     partial = paste0(rand_seq(1, 50), substr(adapter, 1, 14)),     full    = paste0(rand_seq(1, 30), adapter) ) scan <- align_sw(adapter, reads, scoring = c(2, -3, 5, 2)) data.frame(read = names(reads), scan[, c("score", "start_j", "end_j", "cigar")]) #>      read score start_j end_j                cigar #> 1   clean     9      47    53              MMMMXMM #> 2 partial    28      50    63       MMMMMMMMMMMMMM #> 3    full    40      30    49 MMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM

title: Three pipeline use cases
text: Amplicon data collapses reads differ sequencing error observed haplotypes. error rate ~1% 150 bp reads, “haplotype” means “within couple edits” — bounded question. three dominant centroids recover planted haplotypes (18/20, 19/20 16/20 reads assigned). remaining centroids singletons: reads ~4 accumulated errors greedy rule promotes instead assigning — known limitation single-pass dereplication resolved/unresolved semantics least makes auditable (every read either matched centroid within bound visibly ).
code: # three true haplotypes, 60 reads with ~1% per-base errors haplo <- rand_seq(3, 150) truth <- rep(1:3, each = 20) reads <- vapply(truth, function(h) {     x <- strsplit(haplo[h], "")[[1]]     err <- rbinom(length(x), 1, 0.01)     pos <- which(err == 1)     if (length(pos)) x[pos] <- sample(c("A", "C", "G", "T"), length(pos), replace = TRUE)     paste0(x, collapse = "") }, character(1))  # greedy dereplication: each read joins the first centroid within 4 edits centroids <- character(0); assign <- integer(length(reads)) for (i in seq_along(reads)) {     if (!length(centroids)) { centroids <- reads[i]; assign[i] <- 1; next }     d <- align(reads[i], centroids, smax = 4, with_cigar = FALSE)     hit <- which(d$resolved & d$score <= 4)[1]     if (is.na(hit)) { centroids <- c(centroids, reads[i]); assign[i] <- length(centroids) }     else assign[i] <- hit } table(found = assign, truth) #>      truth #> found  1  2  3 #>    1  18  0  0 #>    2   1  0  0 #>    3   1  0  0 #>    4   0 19  0 #>    5   0  1  0 #>    6   0  0 16 #>    7   0  0  1 #>    8   0  0  1 #>    9   0  0  1 #>    10  0  0  1 length(centroids) #> [1] 10

text: text Character vector; row-axis sequences (recycled). pattern Character vector; column-axis sequences (recycled). scoring Numeric vector length 4, named positional: (match, mismatch, gap_open, gap_extend). Recycled single vector given. defaults example, recommendation. with_cigar Logical; FALSE, score end coordinates computed (start coordinates cigar NA/-1).

title: genoaligner 1.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-09-24 Initial release. Edit-distance (Levenshtein / WFA-equivalent) Smith-Waterman local alignment self-contained C++17 CPU core; score CIGAR. Pipeline-friendly, vectorised align() align_sw() data.frame/tibble pair columns; smax-bounded resolution reports unresolved pairs rather returning silently wrong scores.
